children.text: A residence card is a document that grants a foreign citizen the right to settle permanently or temporarily within a given country's territory. This status often serves as a pathway toward citizenship, though how it's obtained and its conditions vary from country to country.

What's the difference between residency and citizenship? First, in terms of rights and obligations, residents can work, study, and access healthcare services, but do not have the right to vote in elections or perform military service. In addition, a residence card may be issued for only a few years, while citizens receive the right to permanent residence and more stable access to services.
Now that you know the difference between residency and citizenship, it's time to learn what residence cards are called in different countries and for what purpose they're issued.

The Green Card is a document that allows you to live and work permanently in the United States. Obtaining a Green Card is tied to certain requirements and processes. If your family member already lives in the US, you can apply through the family reunification program and obtain a Green Card. The same applies to those who already hold a work visa - companies often help their employees obtain a Green Card. There are also special categories, such as religious workers or asylum seekers, who can obtain a Green Card if they meet certain conditions. We also shouldn't forget the Green Card lottery, which gives thousands of people a chance to become US residents every year.

Israel's residence card allows you to stay and live in the country for a certain period, while also giving you access to important social and medical services, making life more comfortable and stable. This card is often issued to those planning family reunification in Israel, starting a new career, or launching their own business.

In Spain, you can obtain a Certificado de Residente after spending five years in the country. This status grants you the right to stay in Spain and work. This card is often sought by those planning family reunification, employment, or starting a business in Spain.

In Canada, you can obtain a Permanent Residence Card if you are employed in Canada, pursuing education, or plan to live in the country with your family. This card allows you to live permanently in Canada, work, and access all the services available to Canadian residents. In many cases, the PR card is useful for those who plan to become long-term participants in the country's economic and social life.

In Germany, you can obtain the right to live and work permanently through the Aufenthaltstitel. If you've already lived in Germany for five years and speak German, you can apply for this card. This status not only grants you the right to live in the country, but also allows you to work and begin the family reunification process.

In France, if you've already lived there for five years, speak French well, and have stable income, you can obtain a Carte de Séjour. This card allows you to stay and grow in France, study, work, or apply for family reunification.

If you have settled or pre-settled status, you can apply for a Residence Card, which will significantly simplify your life in the country. This card confirms the legality of your stay and allows you to live safely and stably, especially if you or your family members are EU citizens. The Residence Card not only confirms that you have the right to remain in the country, but also strengthens your rights and access to various services, such as healthcare, education, and employment.

Australia's Permanent Residency status provides a pathway to live, work, or study in the country permanently. To obtain this status, applicants must go through significant immigration processes that assess their qualifications, experience, age, and other criteria. A successful application allows you to start a new life in Australia, fully participate in the country's social and economic life, and enjoy all the rights this status offers.

In Italy, after five years of residence, you can apply for a Carta di Soggiorno. To obtain this status, you must have knowledge of Italian at the A2 level. The Carta di Soggiorno grants you the right to stay in the country and fully access various services, whether education, employment, or otherwise. This card allows you to improve your social and professional standing.

If you've already lived in Norway for three years and speak Norwegian well, you can apply for a residence card. The Oppholdstillatelse ensures your legal presence in the country and grants you the right to use the country's services, such as healthcare, education, and career opportunities. This status not only provides stability and security, but also makes it easier to integrate into Norwegian society and fully benefit from the resources the country offers.

While each country has its own requirements and processes, the shared goal is to help people who plan to participate in the social and economic life of a new country. These cards not only provide legal status and access to services, but also support the process of social integration.
